"Alex, Jordan, and Sam are standing on the platform, staring at the empty tracks where their train to the coast just pulled away.
Alex: Okay… so that was our train. The 8:15 to Seaview. It’s gone.
Jordan: I told you we should’ve left the coffee shop five minutes earlier. My fault for the second latte. Sorry.
Sam: No point in guilt. We’ve got a whole weekend still. Let’s just figure out how to get there without turning this into a disaster.
Alex: Alright, I’m looking at options. Two realistic routes left. First one: the 9:40 local that goes through Riverside. It’s slower—adds about 40 minutes—and tickets are $28 each. Second: the 10:15 express via the new coastal line. Faster once we’re on it, gets us in only 15 minutes later than the original, but tickets are $41 each.
Jordan: Forty-one feels steep for a last-minute scramble. But I’d rather not lose almost an hour if we don’t have to.
Sam: Same. The express still gets us there early enough that we don’t mess up dinner reservations. We just need to push the meet-up with the others.
Alex: Yeah. Original plan was meeting everyone at the station café at 11:30. If we take the 10:15, we’ll be walking in around 12:10. I’ll text the group and move it to 12:30 so no one is standing around waiting.
Jordan: Perfect. Who’s grabbing the new tickets before they sell out?
Sam: I’ve got the app open and my card already linked. I’ll book the three express seats right now. You two just keep an eye on the board in case anything changes.
Alex:Deal. And once we’re on the train… this is officially a tiny adventure instead of a missed train. Coffee’s on me when we get there.
Jordan: I’ll take that coffee. Let’s go make the platform less depressing."
